exercicio.statement:
Katie and Franklin each brought a piece of cheese to the school picnic. Katie and Franklin brought different types of cheese so it looks like they brought the same amount, but not necessarily the same weight. Katie claims that her cheese is heavier. Is this true?
Katie's cheese weighs 2/5 of a pound.
Franklin's cheese weighs 2/3 of a pound.
Is Katie right?

Read the bottom number of Franklin's fraction and use it to divide the interval from 0 to 1.
Franklin's fraction is 2/3, so the whole must be divided into the number of parts shown below the fraction bar.
Enter the denominator of 2/3 in Franklin's field and confirm the division.

nodes.description: On Franklin's divided number line, mark the point for 2/3.

hints.message: Use the numerator to decide how many equal intervals to count from zero.
Start at 0 and move one of Franklin's equal intervals at a time.
Count two intervals from 0 on the number line divided into three parts.
Place the marker on the second tick after 0 and confirm the fraction represented.

nodes.description: Compare the marked positions on the two number lines.
nodes.instruction: Compare the marked positions on the two number lines.

hints.message: On the same number line, which point is farther to the right?
Compare the locations of the two marked fractions by their distance from 0.
The mark for 2/3 is farther right than the mark for 2/5.
Write the fraction on the left, then the comparison sign, followed by the fraction on the right.

misconceptions.description: Aluno acredita que frações com numeradores iguais, a que tem o maior denominador é a maior.
misconceptions.feedback: Fractions with the same numerator are not larger when the denominator is larger. Dividing the whole into more equal parts makes each part smaller.

misconceptions.description: Aluno compara frações pela 'distância' para o inteiro (gap) em vez do valor relativo.
misconceptions.feedback: The distance from each fraction to 1 does not make the fractions equal. Compare the actual positions of the two points from 0.
